title: The past: irregular preterite
objectives: I can use the preterite of the most common irregular verbs: ser, ir, ter, estar, fazer, dar, ver, vir, poder, querer, dizer, trazer, pôr and saber.
I can recognize and produce the irregular stems (tiv-, estiv-, fiz-, quis-, diss-, troux-, pus-, soub-).
I can narrate a short story or a trip in sequence with primeiro, depois, em seguida, então and por fim.
I can ask and answer questions such as Você já foi ao Rio? using the simple past, the way Brazilians do.
I can talk about life events, holidays and trips in the past.

example.pt: Primeiro eu tomei café e depois saí de casa.
example.en: First I had coffee and then I left home.

example.pt: Depois do jantar, nós fomos passear.
example.en: After dinner, we went for a walk.

example.pt: Em seguida, ela abriu o presente.
example.en: Next, she opened the present.

vocabulary.note: In stories it often means 'so' or 'and then', introducing a result.

example.pt: Perdi o ônibus, então fui a pé.
example.en: I missed the bus, so I walked.

example.pt: Por fim, eles chegaram ao hotel.
example.en: Finally, they reached the hotel.

example.pt: No dia seguinte, a gente acordou tarde.
example.en: The next day, we woke up late.

example.pt: Mais tarde, ele me disse a verdade.
example.en: Later, he told me the truth.

example.pt: A viagem pra Salvador foi ótima.
example.en: The trip to Salvador was great.

vocabulary.note: Always plural in Portuguese: as férias.

example.pt: Passamos as férias em Florianópolis.
example.en: We spent our vacation in Florianópolis.

vocabulary.en: the public holiday, the day off

example.pt: No feriado, a gente foi pra praia.
example.en: On the holiday, we went to the beach.

example.pt: No Carnaval, vimos um bloco na rua.
example.en: During Carnival, we saw a street parade.

example.pt: Fui a um casamento lindo no sábado.
example.en: I went to a beautiful wedding on Saturday.

example.pt: A formatura da minha irmã foi no domingo.
example.en: My sister's graduation was on Sunday.

example.pt: Ele contou uma história muito engraçada.
example.en: He told a very funny story.

vocabulary.note: Regular in the preterite: nasci, nasceu. English 'I was born' is simply eu nasci.

example.pt: Eu nasci em Recife, mas cresci em Brasília.
example.en: I was born in Recife, but I grew up in Brasília.

vocabulary.note: Reflexive: eu me formei, ela se formou.

example.pt: Minha prima se formou em medicina.
example.en: My cousin graduated in medicine.

vocabulary.note: Used with com (casar com alguém) or reflexively (se casar).

example.pt: Eles se casaram no ano passado.
example.en: They got married last year.

example.pt: No ano passado viajamos pra Bahia.
example.en: Last year we traveled to Bahia.

example.pt: Voltei pra casa muito cansado.
example.en: I went back home very tired.

vocabulary.en: to go for a walk, to go sightseeing

example.pt: A gente passeou pela cidade o dia todo.
example.en: We wandered around the city all day.

vocabulary.en: to meet (for the first time), to get to know a place

example.pt: Conheci minha esposa numa festa.
example.en: I met my wife at a party.

vocabulary.note: The eu form is fiquei, with the same c to qu change as tocar to toquei.

example.pt: Ficamos num hotel perto da praia.
example.en: We stayed in a hotel near the beach.

vocabulary.en: to take (out, off), to take photos

example.pt: Tiramos muitas fotos no passeio.
example.en: We took many photos on the tour.

example.pt: O que aconteceu na festa ontem?
example.en: What happened at the party yesterday?

example.pt: Ele me contou a história inteira.
example.en: He told me the whole story.

vocabulary.note: Preterite: fui, foi, fomos, foram. Identical to the preterite of ser.

example.pt: Fui ao mercado de manhã.
example.en: I went to the market in the morning.

example.pt: Vimos o Cristo Redentor de perto.
example.en: We saw Christ the Redeemer up close.

example.pt: Meus primos vieram me visitar no Natal.
example.en: My cousins came to visit me at Christmas.

example.pt: Ela trouxe um presente do Rio.
example.en: She brought a present from Rio.

vocabulary.note: Preterite: disse, disse, dissemos, disseram. In speech, falar is often used instead.

example.pt: Ele disse que gostou da viagem.
example.en: He said he liked the trip.

vocabulary.note: Preterite: pus, pôs, pusemos, puseram. The circumflex on pôr and pôs is kept, and it keeps the infinitive pôr distinct from the preposition por.

example.pt: Pus as malas no carro.
example.en: I put the suitcases in the car.

dialogues.title: How was the trip?
dialogues.context: Ana welcomes her friend Lucas back to the office after a week of vacation in Salvador.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: Lucas, você voltou! Como foi a viagem?
lines.en: Lucas, you are back! How was the trip?

lines.speaker: Lucas
lines.pt: Foi ótima! Fui pra Salvador com a minha irmã e ficamos uma semana.
lines.en: It was great! I went to Salvador with my sister and we stayed a week.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: Vocês fizeram muitos passeios?
lines.en: Did you go on lots of tours?

lines.speaker: Lucas
lines.pt: Fizemos! Primeiro a gente visitou o Pelourinho. Em seguida fomos à praia, e no sábado vimos um show.
lines.en: We did! First we visited the Pelourinho. Next we went to the beach, and on Saturday we saw a concert.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: E a comida? Você provou o acarajé?
lines.en: And the food? Did you try the acarajé?

lines.speaker: Lucas
lines.pt: Provei! E trouxe uma fitinha do Bonfim pra você.
lines.en: I did! And I brought you a Bonfim ribbon.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: Que fofo, obrigada! Vocês tiveram sorte com o tempo?
lines.en: How sweet, thank you! Were you lucky with the weather?

lines.speaker: Lucas
lines.pt: Tivemos. Só choveu um dia, e aí a gente ficou no hotel e dormiu até tarde.
lines.en: We were. It only rained one day, and then we stayed in the hotel and slept late.

dialogues.title: How we met
dialogues.context: Bia asks her friends Rita and Tiago how they met.

lines.speaker: Bia
lines.pt: Gente, como vocês se conheceram? Eu nunca perguntei.
lines.en: Guys, how did you two meet? I never asked.

lines.speaker: Tiago
lines.pt: Foi num casamento. A Rita foi com a prima e eu fui com um amigo.
lines.en: It was at a wedding. Rita went with her cousin and I went with a friend.

lines.speaker: Rita
lines.pt: Eu vim correndo porque o táxi demorou, e cheguei atrasada.
lines.en: I came running because the taxi took forever, and I arrived late.

lines.speaker: Tiago
lines.pt: Eu vi a Rita sentada sozinha e disse: posso sentar aqui?
lines.en: I saw Rita sitting alone and said: may I sit here?

lines.speaker: Rita
lines.pt: E eu disse que sim. Depois a gente dançou a noite toda.
lines.en: And I said yes. Then we danced all night.

lines.speaker: Bia
lines.pt: E o primeiro encontro? Quem fez o convite?
lines.en: And the first date? Who made the invitation?

lines.speaker: Tiago
lines.pt: Eu fiz! No dia seguinte mandei uma mensagem pra ela.
lines.en: I did! The next day I sent her a message.

lines.speaker: Rita
lines.pt: Eu quis responder rápido, mas fiquei com vergonha. Respondi só à noite.
lines.en: I wanted to answer quickly, but I got embarrassed. I only answered at night.

lines.speaker: Bia
lines.pt: Que fofo! E quando vocês se casaram?
lines.en: How sweet! And when did you get married?

lines.speaker: Tiago
lines.pt: Dois anos depois. A festa foi linda e todo mundo veio.
lines.en: Two years later. The party was beautiful and everybody came.

dialogues.title: What did you do during Carnival?
dialogues.context: Paula and Marcos compare how they spent the long Carnival holiday.

lines.speaker: Paula
lines.pt: Marcos, o que você fez no feriado do Carnaval?
lines.en: Marcos, what did you do over the Carnival holiday?

lines.speaker: Marcos
lines.pt: Primeiro eu quis ficar em casa, mas minha irmã disse que não.
lines.en: First I wanted to stay home, but my sister said no.

lines.speaker: Paula
lines.pt: Então você saiu?
lines.en: So you went out?

lines.speaker: Marcos
lines.pt: Saí. Fomos a um bloco em São Paulo. Depois a gente foi pra casa dela e fez uma feijoada.
lines.en: I did. We went to a street party in São Paulo. Then we went to her place and made a feijoada.

lines.speaker: Paula
lines.pt: Eu não pude ir a nenhum bloco. Tive que trabalhar quase todos os dias.
lines.en: I could not go to any street party. I had to work almost every day.

lines.speaker: Marcos
lines.pt: Que pena! Pelo menos você teve o sábado de folga?
lines.en: What a pity! At least did you have Saturday off?

lines.speaker: Paula
lines.pt: Tive. Fiquei em casa e vi três filmes seguidos.
lines.en: I did. I stayed home and watched three movies in a row.

lines.speaker: Marcos
lines.pt: No último dia, minha irmã trouxe duas fantasias e a gente se vestiu de pirata.
lines.en: On the last day, my sister brought two costumes and we dressed up as pirates.

grammar.title: Ser and ir share one preterite
grammar.explanation:
In the preterite, ser (to be) and ir (to go) have exactly the same forms: fui, foi, fomos, foram. Context tells you which verb is meant. If the sentence names a place you moved to, it is ir: Fui ao mercado. If it describes a person, thing or event, it is ser: A festa foi ótima.

With ir, the destination is introduced by a (which contracts with the article: ao, à, aos, às) or by para. In Brazilian speech, para is shortened to pra (and para o to pro) and many people use em instead: Fui no mercado, Fui pro Rio. Fui ao mercado and Fui pro mercado are both fine; Fui no mercado is extremely common in speech, but some teachers and formal writing prefer a. For cities and countries without an article you say Fui a Salvador or Fui pra Salvador.

The forms are only used for completed past events, which is why Como foi a viagem? is the standard way to ask how a trip went. As in the present, a gente takes the foi form: A gente foi ao cinema.

examples.pt: Ontem eu fui ao dentista.
examples.en: Yesterday I went to the dentist.

examples.pt: A prova foi muito difícil.
examples.en: The test was very difficult.

examples.pt: Nós fomos pra praia no feriado.
examples.en: We went to the beach on the holiday.

examples.pt: Eles foram professores nessa escola por dez anos.
examples.en: They were teachers at that school for ten years.

examples.pt: Como foi a sua viagem?
examples.en: How was your trip?

grammar.title: Irregular stems: ter, estar, fazer, poder, querer, dizer, trazer, saber, pôr, vir
grammar.explanation:
Many common verbs change their stem in the preterite instead of following the regular -ei, -ou pattern. The new stem is shared by all persons, and the endings follow one pattern: the eu form is short (tive, fiz, quis, pus), the você form ends in -e or has no ending (teve, fez, quis), nós adds -emos (tivemos) and eles add -eram (tiveram). Learn the stem and you know the whole paradigm.

The common stems are tiv- (ter), estiv- (estar), fiz-/fez (fazer), pud- (poder), quis- (querer), diss- (dizer), troux- (trazer), soub- (saber) and pus- (pôr). Watch the spelling details. Fazer has fiz and fez, with a z. Querer has quis for both eu and você. Poder and pôr add a circumflex in the você form: pôde and pôs, which keeps them different from the present pode and from the preposition por. Vir is the most irregular: vim, veio, viemos, vieram.

Note that eles tiveram and eles vieram have no accent, unlike the present têm and vêm. The preterite also expresses a completed action: Tive uma ideia means 'I had an idea (and it came to me)', and Não pude ir means 'I could not go (on that occasion)'.

examples.pt: Eu tive uma ideia muito boa.
examples.en: I had a very good idea.

examples.pt: A gente esteve em Paris no ano passado.
examples.en: We were in Paris last year.

examples.pt: Ela fez um bolo de chocolate pra festa.
examples.en: She made a chocolate cake for the party.

examples.pt: Eles trouxeram vinho e pão.
examples.en: They brought wine and bread.

examples.pt: Eu não pude ir ao casamento.
examples.en: I could not go to the wedding.

examples.pt: O gerente disse que a reunião acabou.
examples.en: The manager said that the meeting ended.

grammar.title: Dar, ver and the vir versus ver trap
grammar.explanation:
Dar (to give) and ver (to see) are irregular in a simpler way. Dar is an -ar verb that takes -er style endings: dei, deu, demos, deram. Ver uses v- with -i endings: vi, viu, vimos, viram. They have no extra accents.

The forms viram (they saw) and vieram (they came) are easy to confuse, and so are vimos (we saw) and viemos (we came). Say them aloud: viram has two syllables, while vieram has three (vi-E-ram), and that extra syllable is what separates them. Eles viram o show means 'They saw the show' while Eles vieram ao show means 'They came to the show'.

Because ver and vir both appear in stories, link them with the sequencing words below. Brazilian narratives often use the simple past for everything that happened one thing after another: Primeiro a gente viu o show, depois dançou, por fim voltou pra casa.

examples.pt: Eu dei um livro de presente pra minha mãe.
examples.en: I gave my mother a book as a present.

examples.pt: Ontem a gente viu um filme novo.
examples.en: Yesterday we watched a new movie.

examples.pt: Meus amigos vieram de São Paulo pro meu aniversário.
examples.en: My friends came from São Paulo for my birthday.

examples.pt: Vocês viram o jogo de domingo?
examples.en: Did you see Sunday's game?

examples.pt: Ela deu uma festa surpresa pro marido.
examples.en: She threw a surprise party for her husband.

grammar.title: Sequencing a story and the simple past in Brazil
grammar.explanation:
To tell events in order, use connectors: primeiro (first), depois (then, afterwards), em seguida (next), então (so, then), mais tarde (later), no dia seguinte (the next day) and por fim (finally). The verbs stay in the preterite throughout: Primeiro eu fui ao banco, depois fiz compras e por fim voltei pra casa.

Portuguese also has a present perfect, formed with tenho plus the participle (tenho viajado), but it does not mean what the English present perfect means. In Portuguese it expresses a repeated action that continues up to now: Tenho estudado muito ultimamente means 'I have been studying a lot lately'. A single completed experience uses the simple past, usually with já or nunca: Você já foi ao Rio? Nunca fui. Já comi acarajé.

So the English sentence 'Have you ever been to Salvador?' is Você já foi a Salvador?, never Você tem ido a Salvador?. In everyday Brazilian speech the simple past carries almost all of this work, and the compound form is rare.

examples.pt: Primeiro eu fui ao banco e depois fiz compras.
examples.en: First I went to the bank and then I did some shopping.

examples.pt: Em seguida a gente voltou pra casa e jantou.
examples.en: Next we went back home and had dinner.

examples.pt: Por fim, ele pôs as malas no carro e saiu.
examples.en: Finally, he put the suitcases in the car and left.

examples.pt: Você já foi a Salvador?
examples.en: Have you ever been to Salvador?

examples.pt: Nunca fui, mas quero conhecer.
examples.en: I have never been, but I want to visit.

examples.pt: Tenho estudado muito ultimamente.
examples.en: I have been studying a lot lately.

culture.title: Feriados, feriadões and holiday trips
culture.text:
Brazilians love a long weekend. A feriadão is a holiday that falls on a Monday or Friday, or that can be joined to the weekend by taking a single day off, which people call emendar o feriado. When a holiday lands on a Tuesday or Thursday, many offices treat the day between it and the weekend as a ponte, a bridge, and people travel for four or five days. Highways to the coast fill up, and bus stations and airports are crowded, so many people leave very early or on the night before.

The most famous holiday is Carnaval, held in February or March, with street parties called blocos in Rio, São Paulo, Salvador, Recife and Olinda. In Salvador and Recife you can follow trios elétricos or frevo orchestras. Other important moments are the Festas Juninas in June, with quadrilha dancing and food made from corn, Natal at the end of the year, and Réveillon on December 31, when many Brazilians wear white and, in coastal cities, watch fireworks on the beach.

When friends return from a trip, the first thing people ask is Como foi a viagem? Travelers are expected to bring a lembrancinha, a small souvenir. A classic example is the colorful fitinha do Senhor do Bonfim from Salvador, which you tie around your wrist with three knots and a wish.

readings.title: A viagem do Tomás a Florianópolis

paragraphs.pt: No começo de janeiro, Tomás foi de avião pra Florianópolis com dois amigos. Eles chegaram à noite e ficaram num hotel pequeno perto da praia.
paragraphs.en: At the beginning of January, Tomás flew to Florianópolis with two friends. They arrived at night and stayed in a small hotel near the beach.

paragraphs.pt: No primeiro dia, eles fizeram uma trilha e viram um pôr do sol lindo. No segundo dia, Tomás quis aprender a surfar, mas o mar ficou agitado e ele não pôde entrar.
paragraphs.en: On the first day, they went on a hike and saw a beautiful sunset. On the second day, Tomás wanted to learn to surf, but the sea became rough and he could not go in.

paragraphs.pt: Em seguida, os três amigos comeram frutos do mar num restaurante simples. Por fim, Tomás trouxe conchas pra mãe e disse que quer voltar no ano que vem.
paragraphs.en: Next, the three friends ate seafood in a simple restaurant. Finally, Tomás brought shells back for his mother and said that he wants to go again next year.

questions.prompt: How did Tomás travel to Florianópolis?
questions.explanation: The text says he went de avião.

questions.prompt: Por que o Tomás não surfou?
questions.explanation: He wanted to surf, but the sea was too rough.

questions.prompt: What did Tomás bring back for his mother?
questions.explanation: He brought conchas, which are shells.
